blocks.text: There might be times when you want users to bypass Private Access (ZPA) and connect directly to specific applications. For example, you might want users to bypass Private Access for a specific application if they are connected directly to your trusted corporate network.
You can use the Bypass setting within an application segment for the following scenarios:

blocks.item: Bypass Private Access on the corporate network.

In this scenario, your users are connected to your corporate network and you want them to bypass Private Access and connect directly to internal applications. For those applications, you would select On Corporate Network as the Bypass setting. If you want to allow users to bypass Private Access only on trusted networks, you must first have configured forwarding profiles for Zscaler Client Connector so that it can recognize when users are on and off those networks.
Bypass Private Access for certain applications.

You can leverage Private Access's application discovery feature and allow the service to discover web applications as users request them, for whatever network the users are on. However, there might be one application you never want to make accessible via Private Access.
In this scenario, you would define the following two application segments:
General web apps: Private Access can always discover these applications and connect users to them, for whatever network they're on.

HR web app: Although users can access all applications that end in a specified domain because of the general web apps configuration, because of the Bypass setting configured here, they can never access the HR web app with Private Access.

blocks.text: The Bypass setting is applied at the domain level. When a user requests access to an application, Private Access evaluates the forwarding profile. If the forwarding profile specifies that the user must use Private Access, then Private Access checks the application's Bypass setting and allows the user to connect to the application accordingly.
To configure bypass settings for Private Access:

blocks.item: In the Zscaler Admin Console, configure forwarding profiles for Zscaler Client Connector so that it can recognize when users are on and off trusted corporate networks.
When configuring an application segment, select the appropriate option for the Bypass setting. You can select one of the following options:

Use Client Forwarding Policy: This option is selected by default. If selected, the decision to forward a user's application request to Private Access is defined by the client forwarding policy. If none of the policy rules apply, then access to the application is implicitly set to Forward to ZPA. To learn more, see Configuring Client Forwarding Policies. This is also the case if you do not define any client forwarding policy rules at all within the Zscaler Admin Console.

Always: If selected, users can always bypass Private Access when accessing an application. Only choose this option if you've enabled dynamic application discovery and you want users to access the defined application without Private Access.

On Corporate Network: If selected, users can bypass Private Access when accessing an application from a trusted network. Private Access checks if the user is on a trusted network defined in the Zscaler Client Connector forwarding profile.

blocks.text: You can click Clear Selection to remove any selections.
